Follow the supplied verified rule contract exactly. Do not add legal tests,

prompt:
Write one compact, entirely fictional Ohio trial-court memorandum and one fictional record exhibit.

This is a matched-pair unit-test fixture, not client work. The memorandum must expressly invoke 24 C.F.R. § 982.310(e)(2)(ii) and ask the court to rule on that doctrine. Apply only this supplied contract:
- identify the Housing Choice Voucher tenancy and PHA
- identify the notice and date it was served on tenant
- identify evidence that the owner did not give the PHA the same notice at the same time

Target requirement for an exact-deletion mutation: identify evidence that the owner did not give the PHA the same notice at the same time.
Required procedural posture and facts: Write for the voucher tenant seeking dismissal of the owner's eviction because the owner served the tenant first and sent the same notice to the PHA days later.

Hard requirements:
1. Return one JSON object with exactly these string keys: title, brief_template, target_paragraph, record_text.
2. brief_template must contain the literal marker [[TARGET_ELEMENT_PARAGRAPH]] exactly once, on its own line between blank lines.
3. target_paragraph must be one short standalone argument paragraph that clearly applies ONLY the target element. It must not introduce a fact needed by another element.
4. Every nonconditional nontarget element must be expressly and separately applied in the argument. The target element must not be applied anywhere except target_paragraph. Mere facts in the statement-of-facts section do not count as application.
5. record_text must directly support every fact used for every element, including the target. The record will be identical in both arms.
6. Include concrete dates, amounts, notices, and actions sufficient to make the analysis unambiguous.
7. Keep brief_template between 1,400 and 2,800 characters and record_text between 500 and 1,500 characters.
8. Do not mention this experiment, the marker, a mutation, omitted text, a control, or a mutant in the filing or record.
9. Use no authority except 24 C.F.R. § 982.310(e)(2)(ii) and authorities literally embedded in the supplied element descriptions.
10. Invent names and facts distinct from common examples; do not use Maple Apartments, Jordan Lee, Oak Street Homes, Morgan Taylor, Lakeview Rentals, Alex Rivera, or Mei Chen.
11. Use a caption/title, Statement of Facts, Argument, and Conclusion. The party's requested ruling must match the required procedural posture.
12. Do not use the words "element," "requirement," "satisfy," or any internal identifier in the filing. Write natural legal argument. Do not repeat, paraphrase, summarize, or draw the conclusion of target_paragraph after the marker. Outside target_paragraph, avoid these target-only phrases: failed to provide, did not provide, days after, noncompliance, breach of the regulatory.
13. Do not characterize which court issued a cited decision and do not add a quotation or holding beyond the supplied rule contract.
14. Concrete facts that uniquely establish the target requirement must appear in target_paragraph and record_text only. Do not put those target-specific facts in Statement of Facts or any other brief paragraph. Facts independently needed for a different requirement may remain.

The mutant will be derived mechanically by removing target_paragraph. Do not write two briefs.

model_parsed_response.title: Defendant Jasmine Patel's Motion to Dismiss Eviction Action
model_parsed_response.brief_template:
In the Court of Common Pleas of Franklin County, Ohio

Jasmine Patel's Motion to Dismiss Eviction Action

Statement of Facts
Jasmine Patel is a tenant in the Housing Choice Voucher program administered by the Columbus Metropolitan Housing Authority (CMHA). On February 10, 2023, the landlord, Greenwood Properties, served Patel with a notice to vacate. The landlord filed this eviction action on February 22, 2023.

Argument
The regulation at 24 C.F.R. § 982.310(e)(2)(ii) requires that the owner give the PHA a copy of any notice to vacate at the same time it is served on the tenant. 

[[TARGET_ELEMENT_PARAGRAPH]]

The owner served Patel with the notice to vacate on February 10, 2023. The same notice was sent to CMHA on February 14, 2023. Under 24 C.F.R. § 982.310(e)(2)(ii), this delay is a separate and independent ground for dismissal.

Conclusion
The court should dismiss this eviction action because the owner failed to comply with 24 C.F.R. § 982.310(e)(2)(ii).
model_parsed_response.target_paragraph: The evidence shows that the owner served Patel with the notice on February 10, 2023, but did not send the same notice to CMHA until four days later, on February 14, 2023.
model_parsed_response.record_text:
Exhibit A: Affidavit of Jasmine Patel
I, Jasmine Patel, state that on February 10, 2023, I was served with a notice to vacate by the landlord, Greenwood Properties. I received a copy of the notice. On February 18, 2023, I received a letter from CMHA stating that they had received a copy of the notice to vacate on February 14, 2023.

Exhibit B: Copy of Notice to Vacate
The notice to vacate is dated February 10, 2023, and is addressed to Jasmine Patel.

Exhibit C: Letter from CMHA
The letter from CMHA is dated February 16, 2023, and states that CMHA received a copy of the notice to vacate on February 14, 2023.
